neighbours.label: About to say a bird's beak or bill: fires on the word just before 'beak' or 'bill' (usually 'its' or an adjective like 'hooked', 'long sharp') in an English sentence describing a bird's body or feeding. Quiet: the same frame for a mammal's teeth, jaws or claws, a bird's other parts (wings, feathers, legs), and the money or law sense of 'bill'.
fire: The heron stood motionless in the shallows, then struck a fish with its long sharp beak.
An eagle tears meat from its prey using its hooked beak.
The toucan is famous for its enormous, colorful bill.
Woodpeckers drum on tree trunks with their chisel-like beaks to find insects.
The pelican scooped up a mouthful of water and fish in its pouched bill.
A hummingbird sips nectar through its slender, needle-thin beak.
The duckling dabbled in the mud with its flat yellow bill.
Crossbills pry open pine cones with their oddly crossed beaks.
quiet: 비둘기의 꽁지깃은 보통 12장이지만, 이 품종은 20∼30개나 되고 이것을 부채꼴로 펴는 것이 공작과 닮았다.
In his will, Justus, who died in 1827 at the age of 87, left his son Justus, Jr.
The crocodile lay motionless in the shallows, then struck a fish with its long sharp teeth.
A lion tears meat from its prey using its powerful jaws.
The peacock is famous for its enormous, colorful tail feathers.
Bears rip open rotten logs with their curved claws to find insects.
The pelican spread its broad white wings and glided low over the water.
A hummingbird hovers in place by beating its tiny wings very fast.
neighbours.notes: Step-in reader of bonsai1/L34/N7462- (drop 0.17, widened screen --candidates 96). Feeders first: L34/N8684+ and L34/N6051- promote ' be', L30/N6188+ predicts bird 'bill/beak'. Also seen in probing but not claimed: '-to' in X-to-be compounds (0.17-0.78), weaker ' to'/' will' before 'be' (~0.3). Test written blind from the label only; sentences copied unedited. The resident stream probe read ~0.01 on verbatim tops for this L35 pole where play probe read ~1.0, so all probing used play probe.

predictions: beak/bill fires 0.6-1.1; mammal frames quiet; the 'age of 87' leak near miss likely ~0.5; bird near misses ending in 'its ... wings' are the risk.
